head: 14e7bcf650883f0d6c6ad51b9912552093e14164
classification_reasons: Blast radius is wide even though the spec is tight: check_ratchets is wired into CHECKS_BY_PHASE['c'/'d'/'e'], executed by every project the plugin runs on at three gates, plus new git-reading helpers in plugin/gate/diff.py (name_status, tree_files), an extension of plugin/state/unpark.py's risk_hits (shared with the pre-existing risk_list acceptance path) and a new clause in plugin/pr/description.py's _conformance_line.

This is new deterministic gate behavior with no prior-cycle test coverage: the two pure drop rules, the --name-status -M parser, tree_files, the declaration/acceptance paths and the skip-marker scan are exercised only by the tests this same diff adds, not by pre-existing coverage.

spec.md's flagged concerns are all closed and its acceptance criteria are concrete and matched one-for-one by named tests in plan.md's Proof list, which argues for tightness, but the first routine criterion (small blast radius) fails on its own, so routine's three-part bar is not met.
attempted: Re-run context: this is a re-stamp, not a fresh build. Confirmed first that the code diff is unchanged since the prior verdict (recorded for commit 332b399, now stale per evidence/panel/c-items.json's park reason 'verdict is for commit 332b399af5, HEAD is 14e7bcf650'): the only commit between the two (14e7bcf, 'adversarial review (c) re-run for the build commit') touches evidence/adversarial-review-c.json, evidence/gate-c.json, evidence/panel/c-items.json and evidence/hook-log.jsonl only -- no plugin/, template/, docs/ or tests/ file. I still re-did the review independently against the current diff-c.patch and artifacts rather than copying the prior verdict verbatim.

Intent: walked intent.md's 'Proposed outcome' bullet by bullet against plugin/gate/checks.py and plugin/gate/diff.py directly. Every bullet is implemented: check_ratchets added only to CHECKS_BY_PHASE['c'/'d'/'e']; dropped_test_files (D under a test_paths glob, or R out of the globs); dropped_eval_cases (dot-prefixed rename, or no survivor left in tree_files(ctx.diff.head) under evals/cases/, with a partial multi-file delete correctly not a drop); declaration read from ctx.approved_artifact('plan.md') only (merge base, never the working tree) via planned_files/is_planned or the '- ratchet: <name> may fall, because <why>' Proof line; an undeclared drop keyed 'ratchet: tests'/'ratchet: evals', filtered by ctx.status.risk_accepted with no new label; the 15-token skip-marker scan over added lines of test_paths files and the named test-runner config globs, listed in details.skip_markers without ever affecting ok; the new adversarial-reviewer angle 7 and template/REVIEW.md bullet; the plugin.json/marketplace.json version bump (1.0.1 -> 1.0.2, both files, kept equal as test_scaffold.py requires). Nothing solves a problem adjacent to the stated one.

Spec and plan: cross-read every Requirements/Design bullet of spec.md against the actual code, not the author's prose. The check's own git invocation ('git diff --name-status -M -z <merge base>...<head>', 'git ls-tree -r --name-only -z <ref> -- evals/cases/') matches the explicit-rename-detection requirement and goes through diff.py's existing _git argument-list helper, never a shell string. The eval-case 'probe' (appending '.' to a directory path so plan_sync.is_planned's directory-prefix branch matches a folder-level drop) is a real but documented trick and matches spec.md Design's description of reusing is_planned's existing matching. Confirmed every file plan.md's 'Files that change' names appears in the diff and no extra production file does; the plan.md edit in this diff (splitting the combined plugin.json/marketplace.json bullet, explained by a real art.planned_files bug the build session found) is a legitimate, disclosed scope correction, not a silent one. All five of spec.md's flagged concerns are closed with a decision, each traceable to intent.md's own text or the existing codebase, not an unstated assumption.

Proof: evidence/verifier.md is a genuine second, fresh-context pass, honest about its limits (it names three pieces -- unpark.risk_hits's union, _conformance_line's declared-drops clause, and the risk_list-vs-ratchet separate-hit-key case -- as read, not executed, due to a turn-limit stop). I closed that gap myself by reading plugin/state/unpark.py's RISK_HIT_CHECKS=('risk_list','ratchets') union loop and plugin/pr/description.py's _conformance_line directly: both match their respective tests' expectations (tests/test_state.py, tests/test_pr.py) line for line. The only full gate-c.json committed in the diff (1664 passed, 'ran_by: runner') is timestamped 2026-10-15T16:04:27Z and carries no 'ratchets' check at all in its checks list -- it predates this diff's own implementation and is a stale runner record of an earlier HEAD (4b9259e), not evidence about this one; I did not cite it for or against the change, per my brief. Phase (c)'s commands/test/lint result for this HEAD is the deterministic gate's job to produce and judge, not mine.

Blast radius: confirmed no sdlc.yaml risk_list item, auth, data migration, money movement or production-config path is touched (spec.md's own 'Does not apply' section agrees with my own read of the diff). Confirmed no guardrail file is edited: template/REVIEW.md is template content this framework-change diff is licensed to touch (intent.md 'Framework change: yes'), and the repo's own root REVIEW.md is correctly left alone, with the exact owner-facing edit proposed as a one-row table in docs/PROGRESS.md (link, line, current text, proposed text -- matching CLAUDE.md's required format for 'asking the owner to edit a file'). check_ratchets's CHECKS_BY_PHASE wiring is purely additive; unpark.risk_hits's only other caller (plugin/state/cli.py accept-risk) gets the wider union with no code change of its own.

Policies: security-baseline's no-shell-string/no-shell=True rule holds for every new git call (name_status, tree_files, skip_marker_hits's diff call) -- all argument lists through the existing _git helper. data-conventions: N/A confirmed, no new stored field, schema or migration; the dropped-path and skip-marker details are source-tree metadata already visible in git history. No third-party dependency added. Definition-of-done: every new behavior in spec.md's Acceptance list has a named test in plan.md's Proof list before the fact, not a retrofit claim.

The tests: traced dropped_eval_cases's set arithmetic (touched / dot_dropped / survivor_cases) by hand against its four own scenarios (full drop, dot-rename, partial delete with a surviving sibling, internal move) and confirmed each produces the correct result, not a test that happens to pass by accident. Confirmed the riskiest-step test (plan edited only after the merge base still fails the check) actually distinguishes ctx.approved_artifact from ctx.artifact by construction. Found one real but non-blocking nit, reproduced directly in the diff: tests/test_templates.py inserts the new test_review_md_skip_marker_rule_present() in the middle of the pre-existing test_review_md_structure() body, so the old test's trailing three assertions (.claude/**, 'must not modify test files', plan.md) are now attributed to the new function instead. Both sets of assertions still execute and still pass under pytest's discovery -- no coverage lost, only mislabeled -- which REVIEW.md's own bar (style/naming is a nit, not Important) and 'cap the nits' both cover; not escalation-worthy on its own.

Angle 7 (skip markers), newly added by this very diff to my own brief at phases (c)/(d): checked whether a current gate record for this HEAD carries details.skip_markers for me to read. The only committed evidence/gate-c.json predates the ratchets check's existence (no 'ratchets' entry in its checks list at all) and is a stale earlier-HEAD record I do not cite per my brief; no fresher per-HEAD gate-c.json with a ratchets result was supplied in this delegation. There is accordingly nothing live to report under the new angle for this run; this gap is the one plan.md's own Risks section already discloses and accepts ('a dead angle ... not a false park') rather than a defect I am finding fresh, so I note it but do not escalate on it.

Noted but deliberately not used as a reason: the deterministic commands/build/lint and ratchets checks will re-run for real on this exact HEAD after this verdict; I did not re-run them and did not cite any committed run/gate/claude-*.json record for or against the change.
